mujoco_manipulation · feature/obstacle-avoidance

Carrying a cube over a wall it is punished for touching

A Panda arm starts on the goal side of a static barrier; the cube spawns on the far side. Every episode has to cross the wall twice, and contact with it costs more per step than the entire grasp-and-lift stage is worth.

  • barrier — static, 10 cm tall
  • cube — spawns at x 0.56–0.61
  • goal — airborne, x 0.37–0.43
Success
95% ±2.2

100 deterministic episodes on seeds held out from training. The error bar matters here: the training loop's own evaluation runs 20 episodes, and it reported 20/20 more than once — entirely consistent with a true rate of 95%, and not evidence of a perfect policy. Behavioural cloning alone reached 87%; PPO carried it the rest of the way.

What the policy does

  1. reach over the wall
  2. descend on the far side
  3. grasp the cube
  4. lift clear
  5. cross back at altitude
  6. descend to the goal

The crossing altitude is forced by geometry rather than asked for directly. The wall's top face sits at z 0.50, so the cube's centre must clear z 0.52 — above the floor of the goal band, which is why the approach comes back down onto the target instead of rising monotonically.

Three of the five involve barrier contact, so the remaining failures are not simply a matter of running out of time — the wall is still implicated in the majority of them. One episode loses the cube off the table entirely, which is a different fault from the other four and the only one the collision penalty has no bearing on.

How the run ended

Training was stopped at 3.65 M of a planned 10 M steps — killed by host memory pressure rather than by reaching a target or by any fault in the run. The checkpoint above is from iteration 850 (step 3 481 600), and it slightly outperforms the one the trainer had labelled best, which had been selected on those same 20-episode evaluations.

Getting here needed three corrections that had nothing to do with the barrier: the reverse curriculum was handing the policy pre-grasp states the demonstrations never contain, the inherited exploration noise was too wide for a workspace this narrow, and the behavioural-cloning anchor was scoring demonstrations against normalizer statistics that were never loaded — a pre-existing defect that inflated its gradient 41× and drove an 87% warm start to 2% inside 40 iterations.

Rendered with scripts/enjoy.py from outputs/pick_place_obstacle, deterministic policy, 250-step episodes at 25 fps. Success is the latched condition — object within 40 mm of the goal at any point in the episode.
